narrative.overview:
The site reads like a well-kept lab notebook: light paper, careful notes in two hands, and one bright highlighter that marks what matters. Projects, articles and book reviews sit side by side as entries in the same notebook, each tagged with what kind of entry it is. Work in progress is welcome here; the design should make an unfinished entry look honest, not broken.

The mood is calm and tidy, curious and personal, technical and precise. Most of every screen is light grey paper and white sheets; colour arrives only as the highlighter and as soft tints that classify entries. The interface speaks in Sen, a friendly geometric sans; the long reading text inside posts switches to Source Serif 4, so reading feels like reading and not like using an app. Code blocks are dark slabs set into the light page, the only dark surfaces in the system.

This is a personal site, not a company's: never a dark "hacker" terminal look, and never busy or cluttered with widgets, popups or ads.
keyCharacteristics: Light paper background with white sheets that have a hairline edge; they lift only when you reach for them.
One signature accent, Highlighter Teal, used to mark, never to write.
Two typefaces with strict jobs: Sen for interface and headings, Source Serif 4 for reading.
Entries labelled by type with small tinted pills (project, article, review).
Generous whitespace and a single reading column inside posts.
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on every text colour.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Highlighter Teal never carries text; at 1.3:1 on white it can't. It marks backgrounds, underlines and selection. Any readable teal text uses Ink Teal.

rules.name: The Stable Meaning Rule
rules.body: A tint means one thing everywhere: mint is always a project, parchment always an article, lilac always a review, blue/green/amber always note/tip/warning. Never reuse a tint for decoration.

rules.name: The Two Hands Rule
rules.body: Sen writes the interface; Source Serif 4 writes the reading text. Cards, lists, navigation and headings stay in Sen, even inside posts. The serif appears only in article body text and the post's opening summary quote (in italic).

rules.name: The No Fallback Face Rule
rules.body: Never set visible text in a system default face (Arial, Times New Roman). If a component needs a font, it uses one of the two.

rules.name: The Notebook Margin Rule
rules.body: Reading text never runs wider than the 700px column, however wide the screen. Width belongs to the feed, not to the text.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing carries a shadow while the page is still; a hairline edge is the most a resting surface gets. A shadow is an answer to the pointer or the keyboard, never decoration.

rules.name: The Soft Edge Rule
rules.body: Every surface uses soft corners (6–12px) and pills for anything label-like. Card-like surfaces change shape together through `$card-radius`, never one at a time.

dos: **Do** use Highlighter Teal only as a mark: underline, hover swipe, selection, tint.
**Do** set every readable teal in Ink Teal (#007d66), which passes 4.5:1 on Paper and Surface.
**Do** keep reading text in Source Serif 4 at 19px within a 700px column.
**Do** label every entry with its type pill, using the fixed tint for that type.
**Do** keep surfaces flat at rest with at most a hairline edge; lift cards (Card Lift) only on hover or keyboard focus.
**Do** give components soft corners (6–12px) and pills for labels; change card corners only through `$card-radius`.
**Do** show keyboard focus with the 2px Ink Teal outline at 2px offset.
donts: **Don't** introduce a dark "hacker" or terminal look; dark surfaces are only for code.
**Don't** add clutter: no widget sidebars, popups, banners or ads.
**Don't** use a thick coloured stripe on one side of callouts, cards or list items.
**Don't** use Arial, Times New Roman or other system faces for visible text.
**Don't** reuse a classification tint for decoration.
**Don't** make only part of a card clickable; a card that lifts is one link.
